title: Select Tudela Black soybean (Tudela Black): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Select Tudela Black soybean: Yield and Maturity
metaDescription: Select Tudela Black soybean is a grain soybean variety for Mindanao. About 74 days to harvest, 2 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: Select Tudela Black soybean is a grain soybean variety, also sold or known as Tudela Black or black soybean. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2020 as NSIC 2020 Sy 17. IPB, UPLB CA, College, Laguna bred it. It takes about 74 days from sowing to harvest, with 2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Tudela Black or black soybean, this is the same soybean. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Select Tudela Black soybean takes about 74 days from sowing to harvest. That is 10.9 days faster than the average of the 19 grain soybean varieties with a day count, 84.6 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 2 t/ha beats the average of its group, 1.92. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 74 days dry season, 94 days wet season.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took a middling share of damage

blocks.text: The pests and diseases that hit soybean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 11.5 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is black.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 2 t/ha dry season, 2.31 t/ha wet season.
**Fruit:** Black seed, about 11 g per 100 seeds.
**Where:** Wet season (March to May planting) in eastern and central Mindanao.
Flowered but set no pods in a 2023 Ilocos edamame trial.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the black seeded soybean in the registry, for wet season planting in Mindanao. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Select Tudela Black soybean

The registry recommends it for Mindanao in the wet season. Grain soybean goes to feed and food processors, while vegetable soybean, or edamame, is picked green. Pick a variety rated against rust, the main soybean disease here.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is Tudela Black the same as Select Tudela Black?
items.a: Yes. Tudela Black is another name for Select Tudela Black, registered as NSIC 2020 Sy 17. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 74 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
The registry recommends it for Mindanao in the wet season. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Select Tudela Black?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
